plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single plot tracing the flight path of a batted ball across a distance-versus-height grid. The horizontal axis is labeled "Distance (ft)" and runs from 0 to 600 with ticks every 100 feet; the vertical axis is labeled "Height (ft)" and carries labeled ticks at 100, 200, and 300, with faint dotted gridlines filling the plotting area. A teal curve leaves the origin, climbs as a broad downward-opening parabola to a maximum slightly above 150 feet near a distance of about 290 feet, then falls back to the horizontal axis a little past 560 feet, with small arrowheads spaced along its length showing the direction of travel. A leader line labeled "Position of hitter" points to the curve's start at the origin, and a second leader labeled "Trajectory of ball" points to a small circular marker on the rising branch near 200 feet. A short red rectangle stands on the horizontal axis at 400 feet and is labeled "Outfield wall"; the curve passes far above its top. Setting the wall directly beneath the arc invites the reader to compare the ball's height at that distance against the height of the barrier. The plot renders a projectile path in a form that settles whether the hit clears the wall.

interactionPlan.concept: A projectile's flight path is a function h(x) of horizontal distance, and whether a hit clears an outfield wall reduces to comparing the ball's height to the wall's height at one x-value.

y-axis labeled 'Height (ft)', labeled ticks at 100, 200, 300
faint dotted gridlines across the plotting area
teal parabolic trajectory curve from origin, peaking just above 150 ft near x ≈ 290 ft, landing past 560 ft
small arrowheads along the curve indicating direction of travel
annotation 'Position of hitter' with leader line to the origin
annotation 'Trajectory of ball' with leader line to a circular marker on the rising branch near x = 200

movable ball marker on the curve with height readout and vertical drop line to the x-axis
clearance highlight at the wall position (ball-above vs ball-below indicator)

interactions.label: Distance from hitter (ft)
interactions.teaches: Each distance along the ground corresponds to exactly one height on the curve — the trajectory is the graph of a function, and dragging the marker makes the (distance, height) pairs concrete

interactions.label: Outfield wall position (ft)
interactions.teaches: Clearing the wall is a comparison of two heights at the same distance: the hit is a home run only where the trajectory is above the top of the wall

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The continuous arc and a table of discrete distance–height samples are two representations of the same projectile motion

demo_steps.title: Read the trajectory
demo_steps.narration: Drag the ball marker along the arc: at each distance from the hitter, the readout gives the ball's height. The curve climbs to a peak just over 150 ft near 290 ft, then falls.

demo_steps.title: Does it clear the wall?
demo_steps.narration: With the wall at 400 ft, the ball is still well above it — the figure highlights the clearance. Slide the wall right toward 550 ft and watch the margin shrink until the ball arrives below the top of the wall.

demo_steps.title: Same motion, sampled
demo_steps.narration: Switch to sampled points: the smooth arc becomes discrete distance–height pairs on the grid — the same function you would see in a table of values.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Whether the hit is a home run is decided by a single comparison at the wall's distance: ball height from the trajectory versus wall height.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Chart.js line plot: x-axis 'Distance (ft)' 0–600 (ticks every 100), y-axis 'Height (ft)' 0–300+ with labeled ticks at 100/200/300 and light dotted grid. Teal downward-opening parabola from origin, apex slightly above 150 ft near x ≈ 290, crossing the axis just past 560. Directional arrowheads spaced along the curve. Leader-line annotations 'Position of hitter' → origin and 'Trajectory of ball' → a circled point on the rising branch near (200, 140). Red vertical rectangle for the outfield wall (movable via slider), label beneath. Ball marker slider draws a thin vertical drop line from the curve to the x-axis with a numeric height readout; at the wall's x-position show a green 'clears' or red 'caught/short' indicator comparing curve height to wall top. In sampled-points view, render the curve as discrete dots at regular x-intervals instead of a continuous line.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for distance from the hitter: the learner drags a marker along the trajectory, the height readout and vertical drop to the x-axis update, and the parabola's height-at-distance relationship becomes concrete.
- Slider for outfield wall position: the learner moves the wall left or right, the figure highlights whether the ball is above or below the wall at that distance, and clearing the wall becomes a comparison of two heights at one x-value.
- Toggle between path and sampled points: the learner switches from the smooth trajectory to discrete distance-height samples, the same arc appears as points on the grid, and the connection between graph, table values, and projectile motion becomes clear.

authoredContext:
The ball is 141.8 feet in the air when it soars out of the ballpark. It was indeed a home run. See the figure.

Plotted trajectory of a hit ball, showing the position of the batter at the origin, the ball's path in the shape of a wide downward facing parabola, and the outfield wall as a vertical line segment rising to 10 ft under the ball's path.

discrepancies: the y-axis extends to 320 with a 320 top tick, whereas the source axis tops out at 300
an extra teal readout label '(200 ft, 142 ft)' and dotted drop-line from the ball marker to the x-axis are added, which do not appear in the source and slightly clutter the curve's rising branch
the source draws the ball as a small baseball icon; the generated version uses a plain orange-ringed circle marker
the '✓ clears (ball 128 ft > wall 40 ft)' annotation next to the wall is an added element not in the source (though pedagogically reasonable)
evaluation.notes: The parabolic trajectory, direction arrowheads, hitter/trajectory/wall annotations, and axis ranges faithfully reproduce the source, and the ball-distance slider, wall slider, sampled-points toggle, and 3-step demo all work and reinforce the distance–height relationship; only minor additions (drop-line, readout, clearance text) and the extended y-axis distinguish it.
action_items: Set the y-axis max to 300 to match the source axis range
Style the ball marker to resemble the small baseball icon in the source, or at least tone down the extra drop-line and coordinate readout so the default view reads closer to the static figure
Consider hiding the clearance verdict text at step 0 so the default state is a cleaner drop-in for the source image
